questions.text: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

questions.text: What organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are responsible for cellular respiration and ATP production.

questions.text: What is the function of the human heart?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood throughout the body, delivering oxygen and nutrients.

questions.text: What type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body.

questions.text: What gas do plants absorb during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.text: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ, covering and protecting the entire body.

questions.text: What is the scientific study of living things called?
questions.explanation: Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.

questions.text: What structure controls what enters and exits a cell?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, controlling entry and exit of substances.

questions.text: What vitamin is produced when the skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) sunlight.

questions.text: What is the male reproductive cell in humans called?
questions.explanation: Sperm is the male reproductive cell produced in the testes.

questions.text: Which organelle is referred to as the powerhouse of the cell because it produces ATP during cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate energy in the form of ATP through aerobic respiration, making them the powerhouse of eukaryotic cells.

questions.text: When red blood cells are placed in a hypotonic solution, they swell and eventually burst. This process is called:
questions.explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water enters red blood cells by osmosis due to lower solute concentration outside, leading to cell lysis known as hemolysis.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes digests starch into maltose in the human mouth?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin), secreted by salivary glands, breaks down complex carbohydrates (starch) into simpler disaccharides (maltose).

questions.text: The light-dependent stage of photosynthesis takes place in which part of the chloroplast?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll pigments located in the thylakoid membranes (grana) trap light energy to split water molecules during the light stage.

questions.text: Which phylum of invertebrates is characterized by jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton?
questions.explanation: Arthropods (e.g., insects, arachnids, crustaceans) are distinguished by segmented bodies, jointed limbs, and hard chitinous exoskeletons.

questions.text: In vascular plants, transport of water and dissolved mineral salts from roots to leaves is carried out by:
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved minerals upward from roots, whereas phloem transports synthesized food from leaves.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery is the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood, pumping it from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation.

questions.text: What is the dental formula of an adult human with a complete set of 32 teeth?
questions.explanation: An adult human has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars, and 3 molars per quadrant, represented as 2.1.2.3 / 2.1.2.3.

questions.text: Anaerobic respiration in yeast cells yields carbon dioxide and:
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments glucose anaerobically (alcoholic fermentation) to produce ethanol (alcohol), carbon dioxide, and energy.

questions.text: Which of the following excretory structures is found in insects such as cockroaches?
questions.explanation: Insects utilize Malpighian tubules connected to their digestive tract to remove nitrogenous waste (uric acid) from hemolymph.

questions.text: Which part of the human brain controls balance, posture, and muscular coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum processes sensory input to coordinate voluntary muscle movements, maintaining posture and balance.

questions.text: What is the phenotypic ratio of offspring produced in a Mendelian monohybrid cross between two heterozygous individuals (Tt x Tt)?
questions.explanation: Crossing two heterozygous parents (Tt x Tt) produces genotypes TT, Tt, Tt, tt, yielding a 3:1 dominant-to-recessive phenotypic ratio.

questions.text: Sex-linked traits such as hemophilia and red-green color blindness are carried on which chromosome?
questions.explanation: Sex-linked conditions are determined by recessive alleles located on the non-homologous region of the X chromosome.

questions.text: Which plant hormone is responsible for cell elongation, apical dominance, and phototropic response?
questions.explanation: Auxins stimulate stem elongation towards light (phototropism) and inhibit lateral bud development (apical dominance).

questions.text: In a food chain, what approximate percentage of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next higher level?
questions.explanation: According to Lindeman's 10% rule, only about 10% of energy is converted into organic biomass at the next trophic level, while 90% is lost as heat/metabolism.

questions.text: Germination where the cotyledons are pushed above the ground surface due to rapid elongation of the hypocotyl is called:
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination (e.g., groundnut, cowpea), the hypocotyl elongates and brings the cotyledons above the soil level.

questions.text: The second cervical vertebra, which features an odontoid process allowing rotation of the head, is the:
questions.explanation: The axis vertebra possesses a peg-like odontoid process (dens) that fits into the atlas vertebra to permit head rotation.

questions.text: Which cellular component of human blood plays a vital role in blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Thrombocytes (platelets) release thromboplastin, initiating the enzymatic cascade that converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads.

questions.text: In the nitrogen cycle, which soil bacteria convert ammonia into nitrites (NO₂⁻)?
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas bacteria oxidize ammonia to nitrites, while Nitrobacter converts nitrites into nitrates.

questions.text: A state of dormancy and metabolic suppression undertaken by animals during hot, dry summer months is known as:
questions.explanation: Aestivation is summer dormancy practiced by desert species (e.g., snails, lungfish) to survive heat and desiccation.

questions.text: Which organelle in Amoeba is primarily responsible for osmoregulation by pumping out excess water?
questions.explanation: Freshwater protozoans continuously absorb water by osmosis; the contractile vacuole collects and expels excess water to prevent bursting.

questions.text: Primary ecological succession initiated on a bare rock surface typically begins with which pioneer species?
questions.explanation: Lichens are pioneer organisms on bare rock because they secrete acids that weather rock into soil suitable for mosses and plants.

questions.text: The force created by water evaporating from stomata in leaves that pulls water upward through xylem vessels is:
questions.explanation: Transpiration creates a negative pressure gradient (tension) in leaf cells, drawing continuous water columns upward from roots.

questions.text: In the human female reproductive system, fertilization of the ovum by a sperm normally occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Fertilization occurs in the ampulla region of the Fallopian tube (oviduct) before the fertilized egg moves down to implant in the uterine wall.

questions.text: Human ABO blood group inheritance is an example of co-dominance because:
options: Allele O dominates alleles A and B
Allele A and allele B are both fully expressed in AB individuals
Allele A is recessive to allele B
questions.explanation: In blood group AB, both allele A (Iᴬ) and allele B (Iᴮ) are equally expressed on red cell membranes without masking each other.

questions.text: Viruses are considered borderline entities between living and non-living things because they:
options: Form crystals when outside living host cells
Contain both DNA and RNA simultaneously
questions.explanation: Viruses behave as inert chemical crystals outside living host cells, but exhibit genetic reproduction when inside host cells.

questions.text: Which liquid secretion produced by the liver aids fat digestion through emulsification?
questions.explanation: Bile contains bile salts that break large lipid droplets into smaller droplets, increasing surface area for lipase enzyme action.

questions.text: Which photoreceptor cells in the human retina are specialized for vision in low light levels (scotopic vision)?
questions.explanation: Rods contain rhodopsin and are highly sensitive to low light, whereas cones perceive color and detailed daytime vision.

questions.text: An adaptation of hydrophytes (aquatic plants) to stay buoyant and facilitate gas exchange is the presence of:
questions.explanation: Aerenchyma tissue contains broad air-filled cavities that provide buoyancy and allow gas diffusion in submerged aquatic plants.

questions.text: Ultrafiltration in the mammalian kidney nephron takes place across the cup-like structure known as:
questions.explanation: High hydrostatic pressure forces water and small solute molecules from glomerulus capillaries into the lumen of Bowman's capsule.

questions.text: The hormone secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas to lower elevated blood glucose concentration is:
questions.explanation: Insulin stimulates liver and muscle tissue to absorb glucose and store it as glycogen, reducing blood sugar levels.

questions.text: Complete metamorphosis in insects follows which developmental stage sequence?
questions.explanation: Holometabolous insects (e.g., butterflies, houseflies) undergo complete metamorphosis through four distinct stages: egg, larva, pupa, adult.

questions.text: The symbiotic association between Rhizobium bacteria and the root nodules of leguminous plants is an example of:
questions.explanation: Mutualism benefits both organisms: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen for the plant, while the plant provides carbohydrates and shelter.

questions.text: In angiosperm double fertilization, one sperm nucleus fuses with the egg cell to form a zygote, while the second sperm nucleus fuses with the polar nuclei to form:
questions.explanation: The second male gamete (n) fuses with two polar nuclei (2n) to form a triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus that provides seed nutrition.

questions.text: Efficient gaseous exchange across fish gills is maximized by a mechanism where blood and water flow in opposite directions, termed:
questions.explanation: The counter-current system maintains a concentration gradient along the entire gill lamella, maximizing oxygen absorption from water.

questions.text: The viscous fluid present inside synovial joint cavities that lubricates articulation points and minimizes friction is:
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid is secreted by synovial membranes to lubricate joint cartilages, reducing wear and friction during movement.

questions.text: Sub-cellular structures responsible for assembling amino acids into polypeptides during protein synthesis are:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences into polypeptide chains during protein synthesis.

questions.text: According to Chargaff's rules of DNA base pairing, Adenine pairs with:
questions.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, Adenine (A) forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine (T), and Guanine (G) forms three bonds with Cytosine (C).

questions.text: Which fraction of soil water is held by surface tension forces around soil particles and remains readily available to plant roots?
questions.explanation: Capillary water fills fine pores between soil particles against gravity and is the main source of water absorbed by plant root hairs.

questions.text: Euglena gracilis uses its flagellum for locomotion and senses light direction using its red-pigmented organelle called:
questions.explanation: The stigma or eyespot acts as a light filter that helps Euglena orient towards light (positive phototaxis) for photosynthesis.

questions.text: The evolutionary theory proposing that structural modifications acquired through use or disuse during an organism's life are transmitted to offspring was authored by:
questions.explanation: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed the theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics and the law of use and disuse.

questions.text: The unicellular protozoan parasite Plasmodium falciparum, responsible for malaria, is transmitted into humans by the bite of an infected:
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes require blood meals to nourish their eggs, serving as vectors that inject Plasmodium sporozoites into human hosts.

questions.text: A deficiency of nitrogen in green plants typically results in yellowing of leaves, a condition known as:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is essential for chlorophyll synthesis. Insufficient nitrogen prevents chlorophyll production, causing yellowing (chlorosis).

questions.text: Sweat glands in mammalian skin play a primary role in thermoregulation by promoting cooling through:
questions.explanation: As sweat evaporates from the skin surface, it absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the body, lowering body temperature.

questions.text: Wind-pollinated (anemophilous) flowers are typically characterized by:
options: Sticky pollen grains and short erect stigmas
Light, smooth pollen grains and feathery stigmas
questions.explanation: Anemophilous flowers produce light, smooth pollen easily carried by air currents, and have feathery stigmas exposed to trap airborne pollen.

questions.text: In a simple spinal reflex arc, nerve impulses travel sequentially along which pathway?
options: Receptor -> Motor neuron -> Interneuron -> Sensory neuron -> Effector
Receptor -> Sensory neuron -> Interneuron -> Motor neuron -> Effector
Effector -> Motor neuron -> Interneuron -> Sensory neuron -> Receptor
Receptor -> Interneuron -> Sensory neuron -> Motor neuron -> Effector
questions.explanation: Sensory receptors convert stimuli to impulses passed along sensory neurons to interneurons in the spinal cord, then to motor neurons and effectors.

questions.text: Which adaptation is characteristic of xerophytic plants living in arid, desert environments?
options: Sunken stomata and thick waxy cuticle
High stomatal density on upper leaf surfaces
questions.explanation: Xerophytes possess thick cuticles, sunken stomata, and reduced/rolled leaves to reduce transpiration water loss in dry habitats.

questions.text: The maximum population size of a species that a given habitat can sustainably support indefinitely is its:
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity (K) represents the maximum population size an ecosystem can sustain given available food, water, and space resources.

questions.text: Molecules that bind directly to an enzyme's active site, competing with natural substrate molecules, are called:
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors share a similar chemical structure to the substrate and block the active site, hindering substrate binding.

questions.text: Coelenterates (Cnidarians) such as Hydra and jellyfish possess specialized defensive stinging cells called:
questions.explanation: Cnidarians carry cnidoblasts containing coiled barbed stinging structures called nematocysts used for defense and prey capture.

questions.text: Which stage of mitosis is characterized by the alignment of chromosomes along the equatorial plate of the cell?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, spindle fibers pull duplicated chromosomes until they line up in a single file along the cell's equatorial plane (metaphase plate).

questions.text: The hormone responsible for stimulating contraction of the uterine wall during childbirth is:
questions.explanation: Oxytocin, released by the posterior pituitary gland, stimulates powerful contractions of the smooth muscle layer of the uterus during labor.

questions.text: Which ecological biome is characterized by low rainfall, permafrost, and dominant vegetation such as mosses and lichens?
questions.explanation: Tundra regions feature permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost), extremely low temperatures, and short growth seasons supporting lichens and dwarf mosses.

questions.text: The tissue in plants responsible for lateral growth and increase in stem girth is:
questions.explanation: Vascular and cork cambium consist of lateral meristematic cells whose division increases the stem and root thickness (secondary growth).

questions.text: Which mineral element is an essential structural constituent of the chlorophyll molecule?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg²⁺) forms the central atom bounded within the porphyrin ring structure of chlorophyll molecules.

questions.text: In the human digestive system, where does the digestion of proteins begin?
questions.explanation: Protein digestion initiates in the stomach through the action of pepsin in an acidic hydrochloric acid medium.

questions.text: What type of fruit is a mango classified as?
questions.explanation: Mango is a fleshy drupe containing a thin exocarp (skin), fleshy mesocarp (pulp), and a hard woody endocarp enclosing the seed.

questions.text: Which of the following blood groups is considered the universal donor of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Group O red cells carry neither A nor B surface antigens, preventing agglutination reactions when transfused into other blood groups.

questions.text: The main excretory product excreted by terrestrial birds and reptiles to conserve water is:
questions.explanation: Uric acid is insoluble in water and non-toxic, enabling birds and reptiles to excrete nitrogenous waste as a paste with minimal water loss.

questions.text: In human genetics, a person possessing Klinefelter syndrome has which sex chromosome constitution?
questions.explanation: Klinefelter syndrome is caused by nondisjunction resulting in a male with an extra X chromosome (47, XXY).

questions.text: Which mode of nutrition is exhibited by Rhizopus (bread mold)?
questions.explanation: Rhizopus is a saprophytic fungus that secretes extracellular digestive enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorbs soluble nutrients.

questions.text: The respiratory organ utilized by adult amphibians during cutaneous respiration is the:
questions.explanation: Cutaneous respiration involves gas exchange directly across the moist, highly vascularized skin of adult amphibians.

questions.text: Which gland in the human endocrine system is located at the base of the brain and often termed the 'master gland'?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland secretes tropic hormones that control and regulate the activity of several other major endocrine glands.

questions.text: What is the primary function of the semi-circular canals in the human inner ear?
questions.explanation: Semi-circular canals contain fluid (endolymph) and hair cell sensory receptors that detect rotational acceleration to maintain dynamic equilibrium.

questions.text: In plants, the bending of a shoot toward unilateral light is termed:
questions.explanation: Positive phototropism occurs because auxins migrate to the shaded side of the shoot stem, causing accelerated cell elongation on that side.

questions.text: Which vitamin deficiency in human diets leads to night blindness (nyctalopia)?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is a precursor for rhodopsin synthesis in retina rod cells; its deficiency impairs low-light vision.

questions.text: An association between an orchid growing on the trunk of a tall tree for light support without harming the tree is:
questions.explanation: Commensalism is an interaction where one species (epiphytic orchid) benefits while the host tree remains unharmed and unaffected.

questions.text: During anaerobic glycolysis in human skeletal muscle tissue during strenuous exercise, glucose is converted into:
questions.explanation: In oxygen-deficient conditions, pyruvate produced during glycolysis is converted to lactic acid to regenerate NAD⁺ for continued ATP production.

questions.text: Which bone forms the upper arm segment of the human skeleton?
questions.explanation: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, articulating with the scapula at the shoulder and the radius/ulna at the elbow.

questions.text: The structural and functional filtration unit of the mammalian kidney is the:
questions.explanation: Each human kidney contains roughly one million nephrons responsible for filtering metabolic wastes from blood to form urine.

questions.text: Which organism exhibits simple binary fission as its primary asexual reproduction mode?
questions.explanation: Amoeba reproduces asexually through binary fission, dividing its nucleus and cytoplasm into two equal daughter cells.

questions.text: Which enzyme present in pancreatic juice digests emulsified lipids into fatty acids and glycerol?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes ester bonds in emulsified fat droplets to yield free fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.text: The movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential is:
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the net passive movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane down a water potential gradient.

questions.text: Which plant kingdom division includes non-vascular plants such as mosses and liverworts?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes are small non-vascular land plants that lack specialized xylem and phloem tissues.

questions.text: What type of joint permits movement in only one plane, such as the elbow and knee joints?
questions.explanation: Hinge joints allow movement along a single axis (flexion and extension), similar to a door hinge.

questions.text: The process of maintaining a stable internal environment in a living organism despite external fluctuations is called:
questions.explanation: Homeostasis involves physiological self-regulating mechanisms that maintain dynamic internal stability (e.g., pH, temperature, water balance).

questions.text: Which hormone produced by the thyroid gland regulates basal metabolic rate in mammals?
questions.explanation: Thyroxine (T4) controls the rate of cellular respiration and baseline metabolic activity throughout body tissues.

questions.text: Plasmolysis occurs in a plant cell when it is immersed in a:
questions.explanation: A hypertonic solution has lower water potential than the cell interior, causing water to leave by osmosis until the cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall.

questions.text: The primary organ responsible for deamination of excess amino acids in humans is the:
questions.explanation: The liver removes nitrogenous amino groups (-NH₂) from excess amino acids, converting toxic ammonia into urea for excretion.

questions.text: Which kingdom in Whittaker's five-kingdom classification contains unicellular prokaryotic organisms like bacteria?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera encompasses all prokaryotic organisms (e.g., eubacteria, archaebacteria) which lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.text: What structural modification allows birds to reduce body weight for efficient flight?
questions.explanation: Pneumatic bones contain internal air spaces connected to air sacs, drastically reducing body weight without sacrificing structural strength.

questions.text: The Dark Stage (Calvin Cycle) of photosynthesis takes place within the:
questions.explanation: The stroma contains enzymes required for fixing carbon dioxide into carbohydrates independent of light exposure.

questions.text: The structural link connecting a muscle to a bone is a:
questions.explanation: Tendons are tough cords of dense fibrous connective tissue that attach skeletal muscles to bones.

questions.text: Which enzyme present in human tears and saliva breaks bacterial cell walls as a non-specific defense mechanism?
questions.explanation: Lysozyme hydrolyzes peptidoglycan linkages in bacterial cell walls, protecting mucosal surfaces against bacterial invasion.

questions.text: Which gas is primarily responsible for the depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer?
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine free radicals upon ultraviolet irradiation, catalytically destroying ozone (O₃) molecules.

questions.text: In a marine ecosystem, small floating photosynthetic organisms like diatoms are categorized as:
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton are microscopic autotrophic algae and cyanobacteria floating in aquatic systems that serve as primary producers.

questions.text: The functional gap between two adjacent neurons across which chemical neurotransmitters diffuse is called a:
questions.explanation: A synapse is the microscopic junction where nerve impulses are transmitted via chemical messengers (e.g., acetylcholine) between neurons.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries oxygen-rich blood directly from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary veins are the only veins in human circulation that transport oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium.

questions.text: What type of vegetative propagation is exemplified by potato tubers?
questions.explanation: An Irish potato is a swollen underground stem tuber storing starch, possessing axillary buds ('eyes') that sprout into new plants.

questions.text: The evolutionary process where organisms with favorable variations survive and reproduce more successfully is known as:
questions.explanation: Natural selection (proposed by Darwin) operates when environmental pressures favor individuals with advantageous adaptations.

questions.text: In the human eye, what structure controls the amount of light entering the pupil?
questions.explanation: The iris contains smooth muscle fibers that dilate or constrict the pupil to adjust incoming light intensity.

questions.text: Which nitrogenous waste product is excreted in high amounts by aquatic freshwater fish?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is highly toxic but extremely soluble; freshwater fish can continuously flush it out into surrounding water with minimal energy cost.

questions.text: What is the primary role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Azotobacter and Clostridium in the soil?
options: Converting nitrates into atmospheric nitrogen gas
Converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into nitrogenous compounds
questions.explanation: Free-living nitrogen fixers (Azotobacter, Clostridium) reduce atmospheric N₂ gas into ammonia/nitrates available for plant absorption.

questions.text: Which plant hormone acts as a growth inhibitor and promotes leaf abscission and seed dormancy?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid (ABA) inhibits growth, closes stomata during drought stress, and maintains seed dormancy.

questions.text: Which organ in the human body produces the hormone erythropoietin to stimulate red blood cell synthesis?
questions.explanation: Renal cells detect hypoxia and secrete erythropoietin (EPO), which acts on bone marrow stem cells to produce red blood cells.

questions.text: In Tapeworms (Taenia solium), nutrient absorption takes place directly across the body wall called the:
questions.explanation: Tapeworms lack a digestive tract; their metabolically active specialized outer skin layer (tegument) absorbs pre-digested food from the host's intestine.

questions.text: An animal whose body temperature fluctuates directly with environmental temperature changes is termed an:
questions.explanation: Ectotherms (e.g., reptiles, amphibians, fish) rely on external heat sources to regulate their body temperatures.

questions.text: Which respiratory pigment is present in the red blood cells of all vertebrate animals?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is an iron-containing conjugated protein that reversibly binds oxygen for transport throughout the body.

questions.text: During protein digestion in the human small intestine, trypsin hydrolyzes proteins into smaller peptides in an alkaline medium created by:
options: Bile and pancreatic juice containing NaHCO₃
questions.explanation: Bile and sodium bicarbonate in pancreatic juice neutralize acidic chyme entering from the stomach to establish an alkaline pH (~8) optimum for trypsin.

questions.text: The type of cell division that results in four genetically distinct haploid daughter cells is called:
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two consecutive nuclear divisions that halve the chromosome count (2n → n) and generate four genetically unique gametes due to crossing over.

questions.text: Which organelle contains digestive hydrolytic enzymes capable of breaking down cellular waste and worn-out organelles?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicles containing acidic hydrolases that degrade cellular waste, foreign materials, and aged organelles.

questions.text: The type of ecological association in which one organism benefits at the expense of a living host is known as:
questions.explanation: Parasitism is a relationship where the parasite derives nourishment and shelter from a host organism, causing harm or disease to the host.

questions.text: Which segment of the human brain regulates basic involuntary autonomic activities such as heart rate, blood pressure, and breathing?
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata located at the base of the brainstem contains vital cardiovascular and respiratory reflex centers.

questions.text: What is the primary function of stomata located on plant leaf epidermis?
questions.explanation: Stomata are microscopic pores flanked by guard cells that regulate the intake of carbon dioxide, release of oxygen, and loss of water vapor.

questions.text: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA molecules in place of Thymine?
questions.explanation: RNA contains Uracil (U) instead of Thymine (T), which pairs with Adenine during transcription and translation.

questions.text: The hormone responsible for regulating water reabsorption in the distal tubules and collecting ducts of mammalian kidneys is:
questions.explanation: Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) increases permeability of renal collecting ducts to water, promoting water reabsorption and producing concentrated urine.

questions.text: Which plant tissue consists of dead cells with heavily lignified secondary walls that provide structural support?
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma tissues (fibers and sclereids) have thick, lignified cell walls that lose living protoplasm at maturity to offer mechanical rigidity.

questions.text: In human circulatory physiology, the valve located between the right atrium and right ventricle of the heart is the:
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve consists of three cusps that prevent backflow of deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle into the right atrium during systole.

questions.text: Which vertebrate class is characterized by skin covered with epidermal scales, poikilothermic metabolic regulation, and laying amniotic eggs with leathery shells?
questions.explanation: Reptiles (e.g., snakes, lizards, turtles) possess dry scaly skin, lay cleidoic eggs, and depend on external heat sources.

questions.text: The deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) in human diets causes a condition known as:
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from insufficient collagen synthesis due to lack of Vitamin C, leading to bleeding gums, delayed wound healing, and skin spot formation.

questions.text: During anaerobic respiration in human muscle tissue, the net ATP yield per mole of glucose oxidized is:
questions.explanation: Anaerobic glycolysis yields a net of only 2 ATP molecules per glucose molecule, compared to up to 36–38 ATP under aerobic respiration.

questions.text: Which of the following describes the function of red blood cells (erythrocytes)?
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes contain hemoglobin, an iron-rich pigment specialized for binding oxygen from lungs to body tissues and carbon dioxide back to lungs.

questions.text: What type of fruit is a tomato botanically classified as?
questions.explanation: A tomato is a simple fleshy berry developing from a compound ovary, containing multiple seeds embedded within a soft pericarp.

questions.text: Which specialized cell organelle in plant cells serves as the primary storage site for cell sap, pigments, and metabolic waste?
questions.explanation: The large central vacuole surrounded by the tonoplast membrane maintains turgor pressure and stores water, ions, and waste products.

questions.text: In ecological pyramids, which trophic level always occupies the base of the energy pyramid?
questions.explanation: Producers (green plants and photosynthetic algae) convert solar energy into chemical energy, forming the base of ecological pyramids.

questions.text: The main excretory organ in flatworms such as Planaria is the system of:
questions.explanation: Flatworms utilize flame cells equipped with cilia clusters that beat continuously to propel liquid waste out through excretory pores.

questions.text: Which part of the human eye focuses incoming light rays directly onto the retina?
questions.explanation: The biconvex crystalline lens changes curvature via accommodation to focus light precisely onto the retina.

questions.text: What type of response is demonstrated when plant roots grow downward into soil in response to gravity?
questions.explanation: Positive geotropism is the directional growth response of roots toward the gravitational vector.

questions.text: Which enzyme converts milk protein caseinogen into insoluble casein during mammalian gastric digestion?
questions.explanation: Rennin, secreted by gastric glands in young mammals, curdles milk by converting soluble caseinogen into insoluble calcium caseinate.

questions.text: In human genetics, an individual who possesses two identical alleles for a specific gene trait is described as:
questions.explanation: An organism with two identical alleles (e.g., TT or tt) for a given gene locus is homozygous for that trait.

questions.text: Which of the following plant hormones promotes fruit ripening?
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that accelerates starch conversion to sugars, softening of cell walls, and fruit ripening.

questions.text: The structural unit of bone tissue consisting of concentric lamellae surrounding a central canal carrying blood vessels is called an:
questions.explanation: An osteon (Haversian system) is the fundamental functional repeating unit of compact bone tissue.

questions.text: What type of adaptation allows chameleon species to blend into their surroundings to evade predators?
questions.explanation: Camouflage allows organisms to match their background coloration, reducing visibility to both predators and prey.

questions.text: Which organ secretes glucagon to raise blood glucose levels when hypoglycemia occurs?
questions.explanation: Alpha cells in the islets of Langerhans release glucagon, which stimulates glycogen breakdown (glycogenolysis) in the liver.

questions.text: In terrestrial plants, water loss in liquid form through hydathodes at leaf margins is termed:
questions.explanation: Guttation is the exudation of liquid water droplets from hydathodes caused by high root pressure under high humidity.

questions.text: Which phylum includes earthworms, leeches, and marine ragworms characterized by metameric body segmentation?
questions.explanation: Annelids are segmented worms possessing true coeloms, closed circulatory systems, and metamerically arranged body rings.

questions.text: The stage of meiosis during which homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange genetic material (crossing over) is:
questions.explanation: Synapsis and genetic recombination (crossing over) occur during Prophase I of meiosis, creating genetic variation.

questions.text: Which mineral element is required for the synthesis of human thyroid hormones thyroxine and triiodothyronine?
questions.explanation: Iodine is an indispensable constituent of thyroid hormones; iodine deficiency causes thyroid enlargement (goiter).

questions.text: The functional relationship between a specific organism and all abiotic and biotic factors in its environment is its:
questions.explanation: An ecological niche encompasses the specific functional role, resource utilization, and interactions of an organism within its ecosystem.

questions.text: Which of the following blood vessels contains valves to prevent backflow of blood under low pressure?
questions.explanation: Veins carry blood back toward the heart under lower pressure and contain pocket valves to prevent retrograde flow.

questions.text: What type of joint is found at the shoulder and hip, allowing movement in all three dimensional planes?
questions.explanation: Ball and socket joints feature a spherical bone head fitting into a cup-like socket, granting multi-axial movement.

questions.text: Which micro-organism is used in bread making and alcohol brewing due to its ability to perform alcoholic fermentation?
questions.explanation: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) ferments sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide; CO₂ gas bubbles make bread dough rise.

questions.text: Which part of a seed develops into the primary root system during germination?
questions.explanation: The radicle is the embryonic root segment of a plant embryo that emerges first to form the primary root system.

questions.text: The process of nitrogen loss from soil where denitrifying bacteria convert soil nitrates into atmospheric nitrogen gas is:
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria (e.g., Pseudomonas) reduce nitrates (NO₃⁻) in anaerobic soil conditions back into nitrogen gas (N₂).

questions.text: Which structural feature of human red blood cells increases their surface-area-to-volume ratio for gas diffusion?
questions.explanation: The biconcave disc shape provides a larger surface area relative to volume and reduces diffusion distance for oxygen molecules.

questions.text: The outer protective protein coat enclosing the genetic material of a viral particle is called the:
questions.explanation: A viral capsid is a shell composed of protein subunits (capsomeres) protecting the enclosed viral DNA or RNA.

questions.text: In mammalian ears, sound vibrations are transmitted from the eardrum (tympanic membrane) across the middle ear cavity by the:
questions.explanation: The three auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) amplify and transfer acoustic vibrations from tympanum to oval window.

questions.text: Which plant organelle is responsible for synthesizing lipids, phospholipids, and steroid hormones?
questions.explanation: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) lacks surface ribosomes and synthesizes lipids, phospholipids, and steroid hormones.

questions.text: Which respiratory structure in insects consists of branching internal air tubes opening externally through spiracles?
questions.explanation: Insects breathe via a tracheal system, where air enters through lateral spiracles and travels directly to tissues through fine tracheoles.

questions.text: The blood vessel that carries nutrient-rich blood from the stomach and intestines directly to the liver is the:
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein transports absorbed soluble nutrients from intestinal capillaries to the liver for metabolic processing.

questions.text: What type of natural selection operates to eliminate extreme phenotypic variants, favoring intermediate phenotypes?
questions.explanation: Stabilizing selection reduces phenotypic variation by selecting against extreme traits, preserving average characteristics in a population.

questions.text: In flowering plants, pollination by insects is technically referred to as:
questions.explanation: Entomophily is pollination transferred by insects such as bees, butterflies, and beetles.

questions.text: Which element deficiency in human nutrition causes goiter and cretinism?
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to synthesize thyroid hormones; deficiency leads to goiter in adults and cretinism (stunted physical/mental growth) in children.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms displays alternation of generations between a dominant gametophyte stage and a dependent sporophyte stage?
questions.explanation: In bryophytes (mosses), the green haploid gametophyte is the dominant independent plant, whereas the diploid sporophyte remains attached and dependent.

questions.text: The hormone that causes the surge triggering ovulation in human females mid-cycle is:
questions.explanation: A rapid surge in Luteinizing Hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary gland triggers mature follicle rupture and ovum release (ovulation).

questions.text: In a skeletal muscle, the functional contractile unit bounded between two adjacent Z-lines is called a:
questions.explanation: A sarcomere is the fundamental contractile unit of striated muscle containing overlapping actin and myosin filaments bounded by Z-lines.

questions.text: Which marine/freshwater invertebrate group is characterized by a soft unsegmented body often protected by a calcium carbonate shell?
questions.explanation: Mollusks (e.g., snails, clams, octopuses) possess soft unsegmented bodies, muscular feet, visceral masses, and frequently calcareous shells.

questions.text: The main atmospheric gas absorbed by terrestrial plants during photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Plants take in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) through stomata to fix carbon into organic glucose molecules.

questions.text: Which enzyme found in pancreatic juice breaks down starch into maltose in the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic amylase is secreted into the duodenum to continue digesting undigested starches into disaccharides.

questions.text: A cross between a red-flowered plant and a white-flowered plant that produces offspring with pink flowers is an example of:
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance occurs when neither allele is completely dominant, resulting in an intermediate heterozygous phenotype (pink flowers).

questions.text: Which plant tissue is responsible for transporting manufactured organic food substances from the leaves to other parts of the plant?
questions.explanation: Phloem tissue (sieve tubes and companion cells) translocates dissolved organic food (sucrose and amino acids) produced during photosynthesis.

questions.text: The functional unit of gaseous exchange in human lungs is the:
questions.explanation: Alveoli are thin-walled, microscopic air sacs surrounded by rich capillary networks where respiratory gas exchange (O₂ and CO₂) takes place.

questions.text: In ecology, a group of organisms of the same species living together in a defined habitat at a given time is a:
questions.explanation: A population comprises individuals belonging to the same species occupying a specific geographical area concurrently.

questions.text: Which organ in the human body breaks down old and worn-out red blood cells and recycles iron?
questions.explanation: The spleen (along with the liver) filters blood, removing senescent red blood cells and recycling iron components from hemoglobin.

questions.text: The structural pigment responsible for giving human skin, hair, and iris color while offering protection against ultraviolet radiation is:
questions.explanation: Melanin, synthesized by melanocytes in the epidermal basal layer, absorbs UV radiation and provides pigmentation.

questions.text: Which type of germination occurs when the cotyledons remain below the ground surface as the epicotyl elongates?
questions.explanation: In hypogeal germination (e.g., maize, broad bean), the epicotyl elongates while cotyledons stay buried underground.

questions.text: What type of body symmetry is possessed by adult echinoderms like starfish?
questions.explanation: Adult echinoderms display pentamerous radial symmetry, arranging body parts around a central axis (though larval forms are bilaterally symmetrical).

questions.text: The movement of a plant part in response to chemical stimuli is termed:
questions.explanation: Chemotropism is directional growth in response to chemical gradients, such as pollen tube growth toward ovule chemical secretions.

questions.text: Which condition results from a dietary deficiency of protein in young children, characterized by edema, swollen abdomen, and reddish hair?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is severe protein-energy malnutrition caused by adequate total calories but severe protein deficiency.

questions.text: The blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the upper body organs back to the right atrium of the heart is the:
questions.explanation: The superior vena cava returns deoxygenated systemic venous blood from head, neck, arms, and upper torso back to the right atrium.

questions.text: Which enzyme present in intestinal juice converts lactose into glucose and galactose?
questions.explanation: Lactase, secreted by intestinal mucosal microvilli, hydrolyzes disaccharide lactose into monosaccharides glucose and galactose.

questions.text: In modern biological taxonomy, the correct hierarchical ranking of taxonomic categories from broadest to narrowest is:
options: Domain -> Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species
Kingdom -> Domain -> Class -> Phylum -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species
Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom -> Domain
Domain -> Phylum -> Kingdom -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species
questions.explanation: The standard hierarchy descends from Domain down to Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species.

questions.text: Which nitrogenous waste excretion product requires the largest volume of water for safe elimination from the body?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is extremely toxic and requires abundant water to dilute and excrete safely (characteristic of ammonotelic aquatic organisms).

questions.text: The specialized respiratory structures used by spiders and scorpions for gaseous exchange are:
questions.explanation: Arachnids possess book lungs—internal cavities containing stack-like vascularized leaf plates for gas exchange.

questions.text: In green leaves, water loss through transpiration occurs mostly through tiny openings called:
questions.explanation: Stomata account for over 90% of plant transpiration water loss via regulated stomatal pores.

questions.text: What type of skeletal structure is present in earthworms and jellyfish, relying on pressurized fluid within body cavities?
questions.explanation: A hydrostatic skeleton uses fluid under pressure within closed body compartments to provide support and leverage for muscle contraction.

questions.text: Which hormone acts on the collecting ducts of the mammalian kidney to promote sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion?
questions.explanation: Aldosterone, synthesized by the adrenal cortex, stimulates Na⁺ ion reabsorption and K⁺ ion secretion in renal tubules.

questions.text: The process by which green plants utilize atmospheric nitrogen via mutualistic bacteria in root nodules is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert inert atmospheric dinitrogen gas (N₂) into usable ammonia/nitrate forms.

questions.text: Which connective tissue component attaches bone to bone across a moveable joint?
questions.explanation: Ligaments consist of tough, flexible fibrous connective tissue bands connecting bones together at joints.

questions.text: The organelle responsible for sorting, modifying, packaging, and secreting proteins and lipids is the:
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus (or dictyosome in plants) modifies proteins/lipids from the ER and packages them into vesicles for secretion.

questions.text: An organism that produces both male and female gametes within the same individual is described as:
questions.explanation: Hermaphroditic organisms (or monoecious plants) possess functioning male and female reproductive organs in a single individual.

questions.text: Which plant hormone promotes cell division (cytokinesis) and delays leaf senescence?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins stimulate plant cell division, tissue differentiation, and retard chlorophyll breakdown (delaying aging).

questions.text: The outer layer of skin composed of stratified squamous epithelial tissue is the:
questions.explanation: The epidermis is the avascular outer layer of skin formed by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.text: Which part of a flower develops into a seed after successful double fertilization?
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the fertilized ovule matures into a seed, while the surrounding ovary wall transforms into the fruit pericarp.

questions.text: What type of adaptive coloration is shown by non-poisonous species mimicking the warning appearance of poisonous species?
questions.explanation: Batesian mimicry occurs when a harmless, edible species evolves to copy the warning signals of a toxic or dangerous species.

questions.text: Which cell structure regulates the selective passage of substances into and out of the cell?
questions.explanation: The semi-permeable phospholipid bilayer plasma membrane regulates molecular movement into and out of cells.

questions.text: In the human digestive tract, bile is stored and concentrated in the:
questions.explanation: Bile synthesized continuously by hepatocytes in the liver is stored and concentrated in the gallbladder prior to secretion.

questions.text: An involuntary, rapid, predictable motor response to a specific sensory stimulus is called a:
questions.explanation: Reflex actions are automatic, involuntary responses mediated by reflex arcs without conscious cerebral intervention.

questions.text: Which blood vessel branch supplies oxygenated blood directly to the muscle tissue of the heart itself?
questions.explanation: Coronary arteries branch directly off the ascending aorta to deliver oxygenated blood and nutrients to cardiac muscle (myocardium).

questions.text: The ecological interaction where two species compete for identical limited resources and one species drives the other to extinction is:
questions.explanation: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that two species competing for the exact same limiting resource cannot coexist indefinitely.

questions.text: Which organelle is responsible for synthesizing ribosomal RNA (rRNA) inside the cell nucleus?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a dense sub-nuclear structure dedicated to transcribing rRNA and assembling ribosomal subunits.

questions.text: Which structure in female mammals provides nourishment and gas exchange to the developing fetus during gestation?
questions.explanation: The placenta is a vascular organ permitting nutrient, gas, and waste exchange between maternal and fetal blood supplies.

questions.text: What type of food substance gives a positive biuret test result by turning violet/purple?
questions.explanation: The Biuret reagent reacts with peptide bonds present in proteins, producing a characteristic violet-purple color complex.

questions.text: The breathing structure through which woody plant stems exchange gases with the atmosphere is the:
questions.explanation: Lenticels are raised, loosely packed cellular pores in the cork layer of woody stems allowing gaseous exchange.

questions.text: In human reproductive anatomy, sperm cells are produced within the:
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis occurs inside the coiled seminiferous tubules located within the testes.

questions.text: Which class of enzymes catalyzes the breakdown of large food polymers into monomers using water molecules?
questions.explanation: Hydrolases (e.g., amylases, peptidases, lipases) perform cleavage of chemical bonds by adding water (hydrolysis).

questions.text: The term used to describe plants adapted to saline soil environments like mangrove swamps is:
questions.explanation: Halophytes are salt-tolerant plants adapted to high salinity soils through specialized ion excretion and osmotic adjustments.

questions.text: Which blood component lacks a nucleus at functional maturity in humans?
questions.explanation: Mature human erythrocytes extrude their nuclei during development to maximize space for hemoglobin molecules.

questions.text: The development of an unfertilized egg cell into a new individual organism without fertilization is known as:
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction where females produce offspring from unfertilized eggs (e.g., aphids, honeybees).

questions.text: Which part of the human ear converts mechanical fluid vibrations into nerve impulsessent to the brain?
questions.explanation: The snail-shaped cochlea contains the Organ of Corti, whose sensory hair cells transduce fluid vibrations into nerve impulses.

questions.text: Which of the following cellular organelles is enclosed by a double membrane system?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria have both an inner and outer membrane, unlike single-membrane or non-membrane organelles.

questions.text: The breakdown of food substances in the absence of oxygen to release energy is termed
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration (fermentation) breaks down glucose in the absence of molecular oxygen.

questions.text: Which level of organization is represented by the human heart?
questions.explanation: The heart is an organ composed of different tissues working together to pump blood.

questions.text: In a food web, primary consumers obtain their energy directly from
questions.explanation: Primary consumers (herbivores) feed directly on primary producers (green plants).

questions.text: The main excretory organ responsible for filtering urea from human blood is the
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter metabolic wastes, such as urea, from the blood to form urine.

questions.text: Which of the following blood groups contains no antibodies in its plasma?
questions.explanation: Blood Group AB plasma lacks both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.

questions.text: The tissue in vascular plants responsible for conducting water up the stem is
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots up to the leaves.

questions.text: Which enzyme converts proteins into peptones in the acidic environment of the stomach?
questions.explanation: Pepsin works in the stomach's acidic pH to break proteins down into peptides and peptones.

questions.text: The movement of Euglena towards a source of light is an example of
questions.explanation: Phototaxis is the locomotion of an entire organism toward (positive) or away from light.

questions.text: The process by which a plant seed begins to sprout and develop into a seedling is called
questions.explanation: Germination is the growth process of a seed turning into a young seedling under favorable conditions.

questions.text: Which part of the human eye focuses incoming light rays onto the retina?
questions.explanation: The crystalline lens adjusts its curvature to focus light directly onto the retina.

questions.text: The process of maintaining a stable internal environment in living organisms is called
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the regulation and maintenance of a constant internal state within the body.

questions.text: Which deficiency disease results from a prolonged lack of iodine in the human diet?
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency prevents thyroid hormone production, causing enlargement of the thyroid gland (goiter).

questions.text: In DNA, Adenine always pairs with Thymine through
questions.explanation: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds specifically with Thymine in double-stranded DNA.

questions.text: The functional unit of the human nervous system is the
questions.explanation: Neurons are the fundamental structural and functional units of the nervous system.

questions.text: An example of a flightless bird is the
questions.explanation: Ostriches belong to ratites, a group of flightless birds with flat breastbones lacking a keel.

questions.text: Which hormone lowers blood calcium levels when they rise too high?
questions.explanation: Calcitonin, secreted by the thyroid gland, acts to reduce blood calcium levels.

questions.text: The primary site for nutrient absorption in the human digestive system is the
questions.explanation: Villi and microvilli in the small intestine maximize surface area for digesting and absorbing nutrients.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms reproduces asexually through binary fission?
questions.explanation: Amoeba divides into two equal daughter cells via binary fission.

questions.text: The gaseous plant hormone that promotes abscission of leaves and fruit ripening is
questions.explanation: Ethylene regulates both leaf drop (abscission) and fruit ripening processes.

questions.text: The phase of cell division where sister chromatids separate to opposite poles is
questions.explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids are pulled apart toward opposite ends of the cell.

questions.text: Which group of plants lacks true roots, stems, and leaves?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) lack vascular tissues and true vegetative structures like roots.

questions.text: The structural link connecting bone to bone at a joint is called a
questions.explanation: Ligaments are tough bands of fibrous connective tissue that hold bones together at joints.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes carry Plasmodium, the causative parasite of malaria.

questions.text: In photosynthesis, light-dependent reactions occur within the
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll pigments within thylakoid membranes absorb light energy during light-dependent reactions.

questions.text: The outer protective covering of insect bodies is made of
questions.explanation: The arthropod exoskeleton is largely composed of chitin.

questions.text: An association between two species where one benefits and the other is unharmed is
questions.explanation: Commensalism is a relationship where one organism gains food or protection without affecting the other.

questions.text: Which part of the brain controls voluntary actions like walking and talking?
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for conscious thought, reasoning, and voluntary muscle movements.

questions.text: The instrument used to measure relative humidity in an ecosystem is the
questions.explanation: Hygrometers measure water vapor content (humidity) in the atmosphere.

questions.text: The genetic constituent of an organism is its
questions.explanation: The genotype represents the complete set of genes inherited by an organism.

questions.text: The gaseous exchange structure in adult insects is the
questions.explanation: Insects transport air directly to tissues using a network of internal tubes called tracheae.

questions.text: The hormone responsible for lowering blood glucose levels is
questions.explanation: Insulin converts excess glucose into stored glycogen in liver and muscle cells.

questions.text: The female reproductive part of a flower consisting of stigma, style, and ovary is the
questions.explanation: The pistil (or carpel) is the female organ of a flower.

questions.text: The process by which plants lose water droplets from leaf margins is called
questions.explanation: Guttation is the exudation of liquid water drops from hydathodes at leaf margins.

questions.text: Red blood cells lack a nucleus at maturity in order to
questions.explanation: Enucleation allows mature erythrocytes to carry maximum amounts of hemoglobin for oxygen transport.

questions.text: The type of dentition found in mammals where teeth are differentiated into incisors, canines, premolars, and molars is
questions.explanation: Heterodont dentition features specialized teeth adapted for various functions like cutting, tearing, and grinding.

questions.text: The kingdom that includes unicellular prokaryotic organisms like bacteria is
questions.explanation: Monera consists of single-celled prokaryotes lacking a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.text: Movement of plant parts in response to touch stimuli is called
questions.explanation: Thigmotropism is directional plant growth in response to physical contact or touch.

questions.text: The main component of plant cell walls is
questions.explanation: Cellulose provides structural rigidity to plant cell walls.

questions.text: Organisms that feed on dead organic matter and decompose it are known as
questions.explanation: Saprophytes break down non-living organic material into simpler nutrients.

questions.text: Which organelle plays a primary role in synthesizing lipids and steroid hormones in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum lacks ribosomes and is the main site for lipid and steroid synthesis.

questions.text: The main excretory organ responsible for regulating water and salt balance (osmoregulation) in mammals is the
questions.explanation: The kidneys adjust urine concentration to maintain osmoregulation and blood volume.

questions.text: Which plant hormone is primarily responsible for cell elongation and phototropic responses in stems?
questions.explanation: Auxins migrate to the shaded side of plant stems, causing cell elongation toward light sources.

questions.text: The sequence of nitrogenous bases on mRNA that codes for a specific amino acid during translation is called a
questions.explanation: A codon is a three-nucleotide sequence on mRNA that corresponds to a specific amino acid.

questions.text: Which blood component plays a direct role in immunity by producing antibodies against pathogens?
questions.explanation: B-lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that synthesize and secrete antigen-specific antibodies.

questions.text: In human digestive physiology, bile aids in lipid digestion by
options: Emulsifying large fat globules into smaller droplets
questions.explanation: Bile salts decrease surface tension, breaking fats into microscopic droplets to increase lipase efficiency.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms exhibits alternation of generations in its life cycle?
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes like ferns alternate between a diploid sporophyte phase and a haploid gametophyte phase.

questions.text: The structural and functional site of gaseous exchange in human lungs is the
questions.explanation: Alveoli provide a vast, thin surface area lined with capillaries for rapid gas diffusion.

questions.text: In genetics, a test cross is performed by crossing an organism exhibiting a dominant phenotype with an individual that is
questions.explanation: Crossing with a homozygous recessive tester reveals whether the unknown dominant phenotype is homozygous or heterozygous.

questions.text: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood directly into the left atrium?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary veins return freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium of the heart.

questions.text: The structural junction that connects one bone to another bone across a movable joint is a
questions.explanation: Ligaments are tough, elastic bands of connective tissue holding bones together.

questions.text: In photosynthesis, light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) take place within the
questions.explanation: The fluid-filled stroma contains the necessary enzymes for fixing carbon dioxide into carbohydrates.

questions.text: The functional unit of the mammalian kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains millions of nephrons that perform filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.

questions.text: A trait controlled by a gene located exclusively on the X chromosome in humans is referred to as
questions.explanation: Sex-linked traits (like color blindness or hemophilia) are carried on sex chromosomes, most commonly the X chromosome.

questions.text: The type of ecological association between tapeworms and the human intestine is best described as
questions.explanation: Tapeworms live inside the internal tissues/gut of the host (endoparasitism), causing harm while deriving nutrients.

questions.text: Which enzyme in the human small intestine converts peptides into free amino acids?
questions.explanation: Peptidases (erepsin) complete protein digestion by breaking down small peptides into absorbable amino acids.

questions.text: During muscle contraction, calcium ions released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum bind directly to
questions.explanation: Calcium binds to troponin, causing a conformational shift that exposes myosin-binding sites on actin filaments.

questions.text: The movement of a motile cell or organism away from a toxic chemical stimulus is called
questions.explanation: Taxis involves full organism locomotion; moving away from chemical stimuli is negative chemotaxis.

questions.text: Which phase of mitosis is characterized by the breakdown of the nuclear envelope and condensation of chromatin?
questions.explanation: In prophase, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes and the nuclear envelope disintegrates.

questions.text: The vascular tissue in plants responsible for transporting synthesized sugars from source to sink tissues is
questions.explanation: Phloem tissue conducts organic nutrients like sucrose bidirectionally throughout the plant.

questions.text: Which endocrine gland secretes hormone calcitonin to reduce elevated blood calcium levels?
questions.explanation: Parafollicular cells of the thyroid gland secrete calcitonin to inhibit bone breakdown and lower plasma calcium.

questions.text: The gas released as a byproduct during the light reaction phase of photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: The photolysis of water molecules releases molecular oxygen as a byproduct.

questions.text: Which of the following groups of animals possesses a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and one ventricle?
questions.explanation: Amphibians have a three-chambered heart with two atria and a single undivided ventricle.

questions.text: The process by which liquid water exits uninjured leaf margins under high root pressure and humidity is termed
questions.explanation: Guttation is the exudation of xylem sap droplets through hydathodes along leaf borders.

questions.text: Which human nutritional deficiency disorder is caused by severe protein insufficiency despite adequate calorie intake?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results specifically from inadequate protein intake in diets that may otherwise meet basic energetic needs.

questions.text: The nitrogenous waste product requiring the least amount of water for excretion in terrestrial adaptation is
questions.explanation: Uric acid is insoluble and non-toxic, allowing reptiles, birds, and insects to excrete it as a semi-solid paste.

questions.text: Which part of the human ear converts mechanical sound vibrations into fluid pressure waves within the inner ear?
questions.explanation: The ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) amplify and transfer tympanic vibrations to the oval window of the cochlea.

questions.text: In ecological pyramids, the primary source of energy driving all biological food webs is
questions.explanation: Sunlight is captured by autotrophs to synthesize organic matter supporting higher trophic levels.

questions.text: The structure in a germinating dicotyledonous seed that provides initial nourishment to the embryo is the
questions.explanation: Cotyledons store starch, proteins, and lipids to nourish developing shoots and roots during germination.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is vector-borne and caused by a filarial worm parasite?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis) is caused by parasitic roundworms transmitted via mosquito bites.

questions.text: In mammalian eyes, the region of the retina with the highest concentration of cone cells and maximum visual acuity is the
questions.explanation: The fovea contains tightly packed cone photoreceptors responsible for sharp central vision.

questions.text: Which non-membrane-bound cellular structure is responsible for organizing spindle fibers during animal cell division?
questions.explanation: Centrosomes (containing centrioles) organize microtubules that form the mitotic spindle.

questions.text: The complementary nitrogenous base that forms three hydrogen bonds with Cytosine in double-stranded DNA is
questions.explanation: Guanine pairs exclusively with Cytosine via three complementary hydrogen bonds.

questions.text: Which skeletal tissue type reduces friction and cushions bone joints during movement?
questions.explanation: Articular cartilage covers bone ends at synovial joints to prevent wear and absorb shock.

questions.text: The growth response of plant roots growing toward water sources in the soil is termed
questions.explanation: Hydrotropism is directional growth in response to moisture gradients.

questions.text: Which hormone produced by the posterior pituitary gland stimulates water reabsorption in distal nephron tubules?
questions.explanation: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH/vasopressin) increases water permeability in collecting ducts to reduce urine volume.

questions.text: A kingdom containing unicellular, eukaryotic organisms such as Paramecium and Euglena is
questions.explanation: Protista encompasses mostly unicellular eukaryotic organisms that do not fit into plants, animals, or fungi.

questions.text: The primary enzyme responsible for unraveling DNA double-helix strands during replication is
questions.explanation: Helicase breaks hydrogen bonds holding DNA bases together to separate strands for copying.

questions.text: The structural modification of insect mouthparts adapted for piercing skin and sucking blood is found in
questions.explanation: Female mosquitoes have needle-like stylets designed to pierce host tissue and siphon blood.

questions.text: In an ecosystem, ecological succession that begins on previously uninhabited substrates like bare rock is termed
questions.explanation: Primary succession starts in lifeless areas devoid of pre-existing soil base.

questions.text: Which of the following cellular components is found in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells possess a rigid outer cell wall made of cellulose, which is absent in animal cells.

questions.text: The organelle involved in packaging and secreting proteins and lipids is the
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.

questions.text: In saprophytic nutrition, organisms obtain their nutrients by
options: Absorbing dissolved organic matter from dead organisms
Living inside a host and feeding on it
questions.explanation: Saprophytes secret digestive enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorb the soluble products.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes digests emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol?
questions.explanation: Lipase breaks down dietary fats into glycerol and fatty acid molecules.

questions.text: The component of human blood responsible for carrying oxygen around the body is
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that binds to oxygen.

questions.text: Which part of the human brain regulates involuntary activities such as breathing and heartbeat?
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata controls vital autonomic functions like cardiac activity and respiration.

questions.text: In flowering plants, pollination by wind is referred to as
questions.explanation: Anemophily is the form of pollination in which pollen is distributed by air currents.

questions.text: The microscopic structures in human lungs where gaseous exchange occurs are the
questions.explanation: Alveoli are thin-walled air sacs surrounded by capillaries where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse.

questions.text: Which hormone promotes fruit ripening in plants?
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that stimulates and accelerates fruit ripening.

questions.text: An organism that possesses both functional male and female reproductive organs is termed
questions.explanation: Hermaphroditic (or monoecious) organisms have both male and female sex organs.

questions.text: The loss of water vapor from the aerial parts of plants is known as
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts.

questions.text: Which nitrogenous base pairs with Guanine in a DNA molecule?
questions.explanation: Guanine forms three hydrogen bonds specifically with Cytosine in double-stranded DNA.

questions.text: Which class of organisms possesses an exoskeleton made of chitin?
questions.explanation: Arthropods (insects, crustaceans, arachnids) have a tough exoskeleton composed of chitin.

questions.text: The primary site of water reabsorption in the human digestive system is the
questions.explanation: The large intestine (colon) reabsorbs water and salts from indigestible food residues.

questions.text: The type of tropism exhibited by plant roots growing downwards in response to gravity is
questions.explanation: Roots grow toward the force of gravity, displaying positive geotropism (gravitropism).

questions.text: In an ecosystem, primary producers are organisms that
options: Synthesize organic food from inorganic substances
questions.explanation: Producers (autotrophs) convert inorganic compounds into organic molecules via photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.

questions.text: The physical appearance or observable characteristics of an organism is its
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the composite observable traits resulting from the interaction of genotype and environment.

questions.text: Deficiency of Vitamin C in the human diet causes
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from lack of Vitamin C, leading to bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

questions.text: During anaerobic respiration in yeast cells, glucose is broken down into
